correctness.rationale: Splitting geometric cyclic indices at k yields A_r(k,l)=r^-k(1-r^N)(r^N+(r²ω^-l)^k)/(1-r²ω^-l); the denominator is nonzero when r>0,r!=1. A zero requires k=N/2 and an odd l, hence even N only. Weyl double Fourier diagonalization then leaves precisely h=N/2 real degrees of freedom in purely imaginary antipodal Hermitian entries. For two equal-data rank-one matrices, equal diagonals fix magnitudes and all non-antipodal offdiagonals fix phase products; on >=3 occupied indices the graph deleting the antipodal matching is connected. Only an antipodal two-sparse signal has b versus conjugate-b ambiguity. Additional Q using phase i between the two halves determines the missing imaginary cross-term, while one extra scalar is needed because genuinely distinct 2-sparse fibers exist. Independently checked ambiguity formula and zero set for all N=2..16 with r=1.4; finite checks corroborate, not prove, all N/r.
